summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 100 (the early Oct-Nov videos reached 400-680 on YouTube, but later ones collapsed). The best performers show a robot or familiar gadget and open with a surprising 'it doesn't do what you think' line, and the strongest ones earn saves (how-it-works reference) or shares (surprising facts). Generic 'how does X work?' question titles, videos with no Instagram posting at all, and the very latest posts (soil, CO2, thermocouple) are getting little reach.
winningPattern: Maker-friendly subject (robot, clap switch, mic, DHT11, IR sensor) + a 'X doesn't do Y, it only does Z' or 'Without X, this robot falls' contrarian hook in Hinglish, short title with one emoji and #shorts, posted on Instagram first (YouTube is secondary). Videos that show a concrete robot/behaviour (gyro robot, clap switch, line follower) beat abstract component explainers. Shares spike on myth-busting everyday-life topics (sunburn under clouds, soil sensor) and saves spike on robot/maker explainers.
doMore: Post every video to Instagram Reels as well as YouTube Shorts; 13 of the weakest videos were never posted on Instagram
Lead with a robot or a visible demo (falls over, avoids wall, reacts to clap) in the first second, then explain the sensor
Use the 'X doesn't do Y, it only does Z' myth-bust hook, but pair it with a familiar object people use daily
Make series on the winners: gyro/balance robot, clap switch, line follower, IR obstacle robot, and mic/speaker
End with a save-worthy line like 'save this for your next project' or a share prompt like 'send this to your sunburned friend'
stopDoing: Plain 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai? 🤔' question titles with no surprising claim (smoke alarm, smartwatch, TV remote got near-zero views)
Publishing niche component facts (geophone, TDS, CO2, thermocouple) without a robot or daily-life hook
Posting to YouTube only or posting in English without a plan; the one English video got only 161 views
